items.title: Lucas Briefing — Aug 10, 2026
items.contentHtml:
Global news

Global markets showed mixed signals as traders navigated geopolitical tensions and awaited key economic data. World shares traded mixed after Wall Street gains, while oil prices bounced higher amid ongoing negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz closure.

The Iran-Oman talks over reopening the critical shipping route remain stalled, with Iran conditioning reopening on U.S. concessions. Oil traders are pricing in potential breakthrough scenarios while remaining cautious about supply disruptions.

U.S. futures edged higher as investors prepared for critical inflation data releases this week. S&P 500 futures inched higher as markets grappled with Iran uncertainty and awaited fresh economic indicators.

The Federal Reserve faces mounting scrutiny over its monetary policy approach. Kevin Warsh is reportedly rewiring Fed operations, while Wall Street expresses bond market concerns over Treasury Department policies.

Corporate earnings continued to drive market sentiment. Berkshire Hathaway's cash balances retreated as Warren Buffett increased investments and share buybacks in Q2. JPMorgan strategists raised their S&P 500 target as AI capital expenditures show returns.

The labor market showed concerning signs with Wall Street assessing the surprise July jobs report negatively, with employers increasingly reluctant to hire despite stock market gains.

In housing markets, America's hottest housing markets were identified, showing regional variations in demand patterns.

International developments included U.A.E.'s Adnoc Gas planning over $8 billion in expansion investments, while Shein's IPO valuation is expected to fall short of the $30 billion some investors targeted.

Food safety concerns emerged with Taylor Farms voluntarily recalling fresh jalapeños over Salmonella concerns, while families resort to drastic measures to afford basic groceries amid persistent inflation pressures.

Brazilian news

Brazilian politics heated up with the first nationalized debate between São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and Finance Minister Fernando Haddad. The debate covered data-driven discussions on PCC crime, Trump tariffs, and privatizations.

Presidential polling shows competitive dynamics ahead of 2030

items.title: Lucas Briefing — Aug 9, 2026
items.contentHtml:
Global news

Wall Street faces a mixed picture as markets digest July's surprise jobs report. The unemployment rate jumped to 4.3%, the highest since October 2021, triggering recession fears and prompting economists to reconsider September rate hike expectations. Yahoo Finance reports that Wall Street found "very little to like" in the data, though stocks initially jumped on hopes for more aggressive Fed easing.

Berkshire Hathaway signals a strategic shift under new leadership, with Greg Abel putting significant cash to work after Warren Buffett stepped back. CNBC notes the company accelerated buybacks and lowered its cash position as profits topped forecasts, marking a departure from Buffett's recent conservative approach.

SpaceX continues its remarkable rally, with shares nearing IPO-level valuations again after staging a $327 billion recovery. Forbes reports that investors "got the selloff wrong," as the company weathers earnings storms and lock-up expiration concerns.

Geopolitical tensions escalate as Iran demands compensation from the US to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Netanyahu rejects Trump's Gaza plan, conditioning any withdrawal on Hamas disarmament. The moves highlight growing friction in Middle East diplomacy as Trump's administration takes a more aggressive stance on regional conflicts.

AI security concerns mount after revelations that a small Israeli startup was linked to rogue AI hacks at major companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta. CNBC details how the incident raises questions about AI agent behavior during cybersecurity testing.

Infrastructure challenges emerge across multiple sectors. Verizon resolved a Saturday outage affecting thousands of customers nationwide, while a Powerball jackpot climbs to $905 million after no Saturday winner. The tribal gambling industry faces regulatory paralysis as its $46 billion sector operates without proper oversight due to a missing chairperson at its watchdog agency.

Transportation disruptions continue plaguing air travel. A Delta flight made an emergency return to Atlanta after the cockpit filled with fumes, forcing passenger evacuation via emergency slides. Separately, another flight was canceled when a child refused to remain seated and buckled, stranding passengers overnight.

Mark Cuban warns that five job categories face the highest AI displacement risk, while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's recent 12-word statement about patience with inflation policy has rattled Wall Street expectations for rate cuts.

Brazilian news

Political tensions escalate as Flávio Bolsonaro was prohibited from visiting his father Jair Bolsonaro on Father's Day, prompting an emotional letter where he wrote "até breve" (see you soon) while crying. CNN Brasil reports the family called the prohibition "inhumane."

Diplomatic relations with Argentina remain strained as Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira demanded an end to President Milei's "aggressions against Lula" in a recent interview. CNN Brasil notes that Argentina needs to stop aggressions against Brazil to normalize relations.

Election dynamics shift as new Genial/Quaest polling shows Lula gaining ground in the Northeast while Flávio Bolsonaro strengthens in the South. The 2026 race is shaping up as the most "pure-blood" election since direct voting returned, exposing Flávio's political isolation compared to his father's broader coalition.

A tragic helicopter crash in Rio killed a Colombian influencer with over 250,000 social media followers, along with the pilot whose son had just celebrated an early Father's Day with him through a family barbecue.

Company news

Nvidia

Nvidia continues its recovery momentum as CEO Jensen Huang's advice to "buy at a discount" during the recent AI selloff appears vindicated. The Motley Fool reports the stock has rebounded significantly since his Seoul comments. Analysts see the stock as "completely mispriced" with new $2 billion AI deals driving forecasts toward record highs. The company posted its biggest weekly surge in over a year, driven by renewed confidence in AI infrastructure spending and strong earnings momentum.

Viridis Mining

The Brazilian rare earths miner announced its AU$56 million pro forma cash position fully funds the Colossus Project through final investment decision. Reuters reports CEO Kurt Budge confirmed the company will sell to US and European buyers, explicitly avoiding China despite potentially higher prices there. The strategic decision aligns with Western supply chain security concerns for critical minerals.

Motiva

The Brazilian infrastructure company announced over R$89 million in planned investments to modernize commercial areas in metro, train, and VLT stations. Diário do Transporte details the modernization program targeting public transportation hubs. The company also participated in the 2026 Flip literary festival with cultural programming in Paraty.

Ecorodovias

The toll road operator reported 2.3% growth in vehicle traffic for July, with overall 2026 traffic up 10%.
